what_happened: The job added a code-health check, a status table and a 10-landing design review. It was rejected at the final verdict. One of 10 acceptance criteria was unmet: the one requiring clippy with -D warnings, cargo fmt --check and cargo test to be clean. One check failed: the test run. The integration test a_nested_run_works_in_a_scratch_copy_with_fake_agents in crates/athena-cli/tests/binary.rs:169 exited 1 instead of 0. The sandbox's low-disk guard held the run, with 9.0 GB free and 10.0 GB required. The verifier gave two major findings. One said cargo test was not seen to pass. The other said behavior criterion 9 was unmet because its evidence must cite commands that actually ran (D43). The failure came from the disk guard in the environment, not from a code defect, and the record does not show whether the new code is correct.
cause: Nothing checks or restores free disk before the check and verify stages. The test suite has its own low-disk guard that needs 10 GB free. The sandbox had 9 GB, so a correct change could not be proven and the whole job was rejected. Build directories of closed and idle jobs are cleared only as a side effect of the guarded run, and disk is not reserved or measured before the verdict. A disk-held run is also reported as a failed test and an unmet criterion, with no separate outcome for an environment hold, so the job is rejected instead of staying queued. The guard's own message says the job should stay queued, but the check stage treats it as a real failure. The evidence criterion (D43) then fails as a knock-on, since no passing command run can be cited.
prevention: Add a code check before the check and verify stages. It would measure free disk against the same threshold the test guard uses (10 GB) and clear build directories of closed and idle jobs first. If space is still short, the job would be held queued as an environment hold and not rejected. The check stage would also recognise the guard's "low disk ... stays queued" exit and map it to a hold, not a failed test or an unmet criterion. That would stop the whole class: a resource-starved environment can no longer produce a rejection.
proposed_request: Make environment holds from the low-disk guard distinct from test failures. Before the check and verify stages run, Athena must measure free disk against the guard's required amount (10 GB) and clear build directories of closed and idle jobs. If space is still short, the job must stay queued with a clear "held: low disk" status and must not be rejected. When a check's output shows the low-disk guard's "stays queued" message, the check stage must report an environment hold and not a failed test or an unmet criterion. Add tests for both paths: enough disk after clearing, and still short and held. Then re-run job 20261026-064950-38jx (code-health check, status table, 10-landing design review) once disk is free, and have its evidence cite the cargo clippy, cargo fmt and cargo test commands that actually ran.
